texto: In Dutch, the regular present is formed with the root for «ik» (werk, woon, kook), the root + -t for «jij/hij/zij» (werkt, woont, kookt) and the form in -in for the plurals «wij/jullie/zij» (werken, wonen, koken). If the sentence begins with a circumstantial complement of time or place («Elke dag...», «Na het werk...»), the conjugated verb is held in second position and the subject is moved to the third (investment subject-verb).

frases.nl: Ik woon in Utrecht en ik werk in een café.
frases.es: Vivo en Utrecht y trabajo en una cafetería.
frases.en: I live in Utrecht and work in a cafe.

frases.nl: Mijn broer leert Nederlands op school.
frases.es: Mi hermano aprende neerlandés en la escuela.
frases.en: My brother learns Dutch at school.

frases.nl: Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis.
frases.es: Después del trabajo mi hermano cocina en casa.
frases.en: After work my brother cooks at home.

frases.nl: In het weekend bezoeken we onze vrienden.
frases.es: El fin de semana visitamos a nuestros amigos.
frases.en: We visited our friends on the weekend.

bloques.pregunta: What termination does the verbal root receive in present with the subject «hij» (my brother)?

opciones.texto: Add -t to the root of the verb
opciones.explicacion: «Koken» has «kook» root and with «mijn broer» (hij) da «kookt».

opciones.texto: It is added - as in the plural
opciones.explicacion: The completion - is reserved for the forms of the plural (wij, jullie, zij).

opciones.texto: The root is left naked without any disinence
opciones.explicacion: The root alone corresponds to the first person «ik».

bloques.pregunta: What does the brother do after the working day?
bloques.frase: Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis.

opciones.explicacion: «Kookt» is kitchen and «thuis» is at home.

opciones.texto: He's going to a coffee in Utrecht with friends.
opciones.explicacion: It combines the brother's workplace with the later activity.
The school study is mentioned in the previous sentence.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the correct verbal form for the «wij» subject.

opciones.explicacion: With the plural pronoun «wij» the verb takes the full form with -in.

bloques.pregunta: Why is the verb «kookt» going before «mijn broer» in «Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis»?

opciones.texto: Because at the beginning of the prayer with a circumstantial complement, there is compulsory investment.
opciones.explicacion: In Dutch, the finite verb always occupies the second syntactic position (rule V2).

opciones.texto: Because it's an indirect question phrase.
opciones.explicacion: It is not a question, but a statement with a syntactic investment.

opciones.texto: Porque el sujeto «mijn broer» es un pronombre tónico
opciones.explicacion: The investment depends on the structure of the phrase, not the type of noun.

bloques.pregunta: What activity do you do during the weekend?
bloques.frase: In het weekend bezoeken we onze vrienden.

opciones.explicacion: «Bezoeken» means to visit and «onze vrienden» our friends.

opciones.texto: They work together in the cafeteria.
opciones.explicacion: The text indicates that they work on working days and the weekend have social time.

opciones.texto: They stay resting in the garden.
opciones.explicacion: It does not mention resting in the garden, but visiting friendships.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the verb of first person residence.
bloques.frase: Ik ___ in Utrecht en ik werk in een café.

opciones.explicacion: With «ik» the direct verbal root is used («wonen» - h. «woon»).
It carries the second and third-person -t singular («hij woont»).
It is the infinitive or plural form («wij wonen»).

bloques.frase: Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis
bloques.traduccion: After work my brother cooks at home.
bloques.explicacion: Initial time supplement, second position verb and subject investment.

intro: It builds affirmative phrases in the present with daily verbs and respects the V2 position.
